# [US-010] Minify CSS, JavaScript, HTML and SVG files

> **Epic:** BP2 (see [EPIC-BP2-conventions.md](EPIC-BP2-conventions.md))
> **Rule:** `MinifyTextFiles`, "Minifier les fichiers CSS, JavaScript, HTML et SVG", category `network`
> **Status:** DONE (automated gates passed, manual browser checks pending; see `docs/reviews/REVIEW-US-006-014.md`)

## 1. User Story Statement

**As an** eco-design auditor,
**I want** each page to report the CSS, JavaScript, HTML and SVG files that are not minified,
**So that** the site owner can add minification to the build and reduce the weight of text resources.

## 2. Context & Detailed Description

### Files checked

- **Types:** the same text-file detection as US-008: HTML, CSS, JS and SVG, by MIME type, else by extension.
- **Status:** 2xx responses only.
- **Size:** files of **1 000 bytes or more**, decoded. This was a product decision.

### File contents

This was a product decision.

- The contents come **only from what DevTools captured** for the page (`getContent()`). **Nothing is re-downloaded.**
- Files whose content is unavailable are **"non évaluées"**. They are excluded from the grade and counted in the detail as "(N fichiers non évalués)".
- Files over **5 MB** are not analysed and are counted as non évalués.

### Minification heuristic

This was a product decision; the thresholds are PO defaults. A file is **minified** when its **removable bytes are under 5 % of its size**.

**Removable bytes** are:

- **comments** (`/* … */` in CSS and JS, `<!-- … -->` in HTML and SVG, `// …` line comments in JS), **except**:
  - licence comments starting with `/*!` or containing `@license` or `@preserve`;
  - `//# sourceMappingURL=…` and `/*# sourceMappingURL=… */`;
- **whitespace that could be removed:** every run of whitespace (spaces, tabs, line breaks) longer than one character counts for its length minus 1, plus every line break.

A required single space ("var a", "@media screen") is **not** counted. The heuristic must not try to parse strings perfectly: it is an estimate, and the 5 % tolerance absorbs edge cases such as `/*` inside strings, `<pre>` blocks and template literals.

The exact algorithm is the team lead's choice, provided it classifies the reference fixtures below correctly.

### Reference fixtures

These must be part of the tests.

| Fixture | Expected |
|---|---|
| A real minified library (e.g. a `*.min.js` and a `*.min.css` of a popular library, vendored as test fixtures) | minified |
| The same library unminified | not minified |
| Minified JS with a `/*! license */` header and a `sourceMappingURL` comment | minified |
| A server-rendered HTML page with indentation | not minified |
| An SVG exported from a design tool with indentation and comments | not minified |

### Grade

These follow the request; the worst grade wins.

- **C:** there is at least one evaluated file and **none** is minified.
- **B:** at least one evaluated file is not minified, but not all.
- **A:** all evaluated files are minified, or there is no checked file.
- **Non évaluée:** there are files in scope, but **none** could be evaluated (no content captured), for example "Contenu des fichiers non disponible".

### Offender lines

- Format: `<display name> (<type>, <size in ko>) : non minifié (~<p> % d'octets superflus)`.
- Sorted by superfluous bytes, largest first.

### Asynchronous behaviour

- Reading contents is asynchronous. While contents are still being read for a page, the rule shows **"Analyse en cours… (n/N fichiers)"** and no grade, like the image estimations (ARCH-DECISION-007).
- It updates by itself.
- Stopping the analysis saves the page immediately. Unread files become non évalués with the reason "analyse arrêtée".

## 3. Tech Stack Hints & Scope Constraints

- **In scope:**
  - reading captured contents;
  - the heuristic as a pure, unit-tested function;
  - the rule;
  - the progress state.
- **Out of scope:**
  - estimating the gain in kB;
  - re-downloading;
  - inline `<script>` and `<style>` blocks inside the HTML (the HTML file itself is checked as a whole);
  - JSON.
- **Architecture hints for the team lead (not decisions):**
  - `evaluate` is synchronous (ARCH-DECISION-004). Reading contents fits the asynchronous "estimations" mechanism of ARCH-DECISION-007, generalised from images to text contents, or a similar job queue.
  - `ExtensionBrowser.getResourceContent` already caches DevTools contents. Check that it covers text resources and not only images, and that its memory bound still holds.
  - Text content arrives as text or base64. Decode it with the response charset, defaulting to UTF-8.
  - Running the heuristic on a large file must not block the panel: no main-thread task over 50 ms. Chunk the work or use a worker.
- **State:** per file `pending | evaluated | not-evaluated(reason)`; per rule "Analyse en cours…" until settled.
- **Persistence:** the rule result is stored with the page. Contents are **never** persisted.

## 4. Acceptance Criteria (Gherkin Scenarios)

### Scenario 1: Happy path: all files minified
Given the page loaded "app.min.js" (120 kB) and "style.min.css" (30 kB), with captured contents, both minified
When the best practices are evaluated
Then the rule is graded "A"

### Scenario 2: One unminified file gives B
Given "app.min.js" is minified and "custom.css" (15 kB) has indentation and comments making 22 % of its bytes
When the best practices are evaluated
Then the rule is graded "B"
And the line "custom.css (CSS, 15 ko) : non minifié (~22 % d'octets superflus)" is listed

### Scenario 3: Nothing minified gives C
Given the 3 evaluated text files of the page are all not minified
When the best practices are evaluated
Then the rule is graded "C"

### Scenario 4: Licence and source-map comments are tolerated
Given a minified JS file starting with "/*! lib v1.0 | MIT */" and ending with "//# sourceMappingURL=app.js.map"
When the file is analysed
Then it is classified as minified

### Scenario 5: Reference fixtures
Given the reference fixtures of §2
When each is analysed
Then each classification matches the expected column

### Scenario 6: Content not captured
Given 4 text files are in scope and DevTools captured the content of only 2
When the best practices are evaluated
Then the grade uses the 2 evaluated files
And the detail mentions "(2 fichiers non évalués)"

### Scenario 7: No content available at all
Given text files are in scope but no content was captured
When the best practices are evaluated
Then the rule shows "Non évaluée" with the detail "Contenu des fichiers non disponible"

### Scenario 8: Small and large files
Given a 700-byte unminified CSS file and an 8 MB JS file
When the best practices are evaluated
Then the CSS file is ignored and the JS file is counted as non évalué

### Scenario 9: Contents being read
Given 5 text files of the page whose contents are still being read, 2 already analysed
When the auditor looks at the rule
Then it shows "Analyse en cours… (2/5 fichiers)" and no grade
And it updates without user action

### Scenario 10: Stop during analysis
Given 3 files are still pending
When the auditor clicks "Stopper l'analyse"
Then the analysis is saved immediately and the 3 files are non évalués ("analyse arrêtée")

### Scenario 11: Nothing is re-downloaded
Given a text file loaded before the recording started, whose content DevTools did not capture
When the best practices are evaluated
Then no network request is made for it, and it is non évalué

## 5. Non-Functional Requirements (NFRs) & Constraints

- **Responsiveness:** no main-thread task over 50 ms caused by the heuristic. A 5 MB file is analysed in under 500 ms in total.
- **Sobriety:** each file content is read and analysed once per URL per analysis. Contents are released after analysis.
- **Privacy:** contents never leave the browser and are never persisted. No network request is made.

## 6. Definition of Ready (DoR) Checklist

- [x] User story statement follows the standard format.
- [x] Written in `docs/stories/US-010.md`.
- [x] Happy path (1), alternative paths (4, 5, 6, 11) and edge cases (2, 3, 7, 8, 9, 10) in Gherkin.
- [x] Data states: per file `pending | evaluated | not-evaluated`; per rule "Analyse en cours…".
- [x] Persistence: rule result only; contents never persisted.
- [x] Product decisions recorded:
  - heuristic with 5 % tolerance (PO default threshold);
  - files under 1 kB ignored;
  - DevTools content only, no re-download;
  - 5 MB cap.
